<description>
This doesn't fix the general case of rebroadcasting potentially surprising users by divulging the originator IP trivially, but for users opting into private broadcast, it seems a bridge too far for them to expect the current behavior.

e.g. an incoming dust payment triggering your node to rebroadcast 24-36th later over clearnet

This can be removed if/when wallet drives through private broadcast.

see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/3828 for running broader issue
</description>

[2026-09-28] r:5345286414 review COMMENTED by mzumsande (member) (edited 2026-09-28):
[quoted text omitted]

I think that promoting private broadcast into an essential feature (and with it, connectivity to privacy networks) that is required for basic functionality such as rebroadcasting is a major change that needs to be very well discussed, to say the least.

As of now I view it as an optional feature.

But as such, I could see users starting with `-privatebroadcast` just to send out some transactions, and then restarting back to regular mode without private broadcast with a wallet that rebroadcasts them. This could reveal the origin of their transactions after the fact, so there is only so much this PR can achieve.

I would personally be in favor of dropping wallet rebroadcasting completely, it is a massive privacy footgun for non-privatebroadcast users as well, for little benefit.
